//: HAND-CURATED PARSER RULES. Contains rules, not shapes -- the markdown in
docs/shape-libraries/ stays the source of truth for what shapes exist, and
scripts/buildShapeIndex.js reads this to know HOW to read each file.
`find`/`into` exist because only 17 of the 30 Usage blocks contain a literal
{shape} placeholder; the other 13 show a worked example instead. Rather than
hard-coding 13 style templates here (which would go stale invisibly when the
markdown changed), we record the exact substring the example occupies and let
the generator punch the hole. If `find` ever stops appearing in its Usage
block the build FAILS -- staleness is loud by construction.
`mode` selects the harvester: flat | sectioned | sectionedVendor | manual.
`coverage` is reported to the caller verbatim and gates the validator's

azure2.title: Azure (2021+ icon set)
azure2.//: Hybrid file: a `## Shapes (648)` header, then `### category (N)` bullet sections, then a `### Additional Categories` block of unbackticked comma lists. Flattening to the bullets alone loses 294 shapes, so both passes run. Tokens are category-qualified ('compute/Virtual_Machine') because the same slug appears in several categories.
azure2.note: 513 of the 648 shapes draw.io ships are indexed here. An unlisted icon may still exist -- the path form is img/lib/azure2/{category}/{Name}.svg.

bpmn.title: BPMN 2.0
bpmn.//: The `## Parameters` section's bullets (`outline`, `symbol`) are style KEYS, not shapes. Section-scoped harvesting excludes them without a special case; `params` re-surfaces them to the caller as what they are.

electrical.title: Electrical / electronic symbols
electrical.//: Addressing is category-qualified: mxgraph.electrical.{category}.{shape}. A flat list would emit mxgraph.electrical.resistor_1, which draw.io does not resolve.
electrical.note: A representative sample only -- draw.io ships roughly 50 categories. The addressing form is mxgraph.electrical.{category}.{shape}.

fluidpower.title: Fluid power
fluidpower.note: Shapes are numbered (x10010, x10020, ...) rather than named.

infographic.title: Infographic
infographic.//: Bullets carry per-shape extra style params: `shadedCube` (needs `isoAngle=15;`). The generator folds those into that shape's emitted style, so the caller still copies one finished string.

material_design.title: Google Material Icons
material_design.//: Sections are h2 (`## action (115)`), not h3, and are purely organisational -- the CDN URL takes a bare icon name, so tokens are NOT category-qualified. Icons load from fonts.gstatic.com at render time.
material_design.note: 300 common icons of the ~2,100 Material set. Any Material icon name works in the same URL, whether or not it is listed here.

mscae.title: Microsoft Azure / Cloud & Enterprise (legacy)
mscae.//: Unindexable from this file: addressing needs mxgraph.mscae.{category}.{shape} and the source never attributes its three bullets to a category. They are therefore carried as manual entries and coverage says so.
mscae.note: Not indexed. Shapes are mxgraph.mscae.{category}.{shape} with category one of cloud, intune, oms, system_center. Prefer the azure2 library for current Azure diagrams.

network.title: Networking
network.//: Library name is `network` but the mxgraph prefix is `networks`. Never derive a prefix from a filename.

pid.title: P&ID (piping and instrumentation)
pid.//: The only parametric library: one valve shape specialised by `valveType=`, so the file has no shape bullets at all. Entries are written out here by hand.

shapes.name: pid2valves.valve
shapes.note: valveType= is required; the emitted style defaults it to gate. Swap in any value from params.valveType.

pid.note: Parametric rather than enumerated: one valve shape specialised by valveType=, plus three instrument shapes. Swap the valveType value rather than looking for a differently-named valve shape.

rack.title: Server racks
rack.//: Three levels of qualification: `### Vendor` (lowercased, spaces to underscores), an optional `**subcategory:**` bold pseudo-heading beneath it, then the model. `### General (rackGeneral)` is not a vendor at all -- it switches the mxgraph LIBRARY to mxgraph.rackGeneral, so those shapes carry their own style template.
rack.note: A representative sample of draw.io's rack library. Addressing is mxgraph.rack.{vendor}.{model}, or mxgraph.rack.{vendor}.{category}.{model} where a vendor has subcategories.

sap.title: SAP
sap.note: Some shape names are bare numbers (1-13). They are names, not indices.
